The active-set solver hit a singular KKT matrix in the cross-check's random problems. Why singular? The KKT is [H_FF, P; P^T, 0] — singular iff P loses column rank, i.e., a commodity in tidx has NO free slot. In the cross-check, slot_com is arbitrary (n slots over m commodities) and mode could be 'admit' — in admit, T can include a commodity whose all slots are in Z... wait, I argued this can't happen in admit because T gains k only at X_k = d_k > 0. Hmm — but what about the initial state in ADMIT: Z = all slots, T = ∅. Fine.

Ah wait — but in the cross-check, dv are random ≥ 1, so d_k > 0. Let me think where the singularity arises... The active-set adds a commodity to T when a_k == alpha with slope > 0. At that point X_k = d_k with a positive slot... hmm, could all its positive slots simultaneously be added to Z at the same alpha? For k ∈ T_new (just added), its slots: slope_k > 0, so at the step end X_k = d_k. But individual slots might hit zero at the same alpha — they'd also be added to Z. Could ALL slots of k hit zero at the same alpha while X_k = d_k > 0? X_k becomes d_k = X_k + alpha*slope_k > 0 so not all slots are zero... but wait: slots not in Z can be zero transiently? The step: x = x + alpha*p. Slots blocked with a_s == alpha get x=0 and Z. Slots NOT blocked stay positive (a_s > alpha → x_s + alpha*p_s > 0 ✓). So at the end, X_k = d_k > 0 means at least one slot positive → not in Z ✓. Hmm, then free slots exist for k.

Unless... alpha == 1.0 branch: x = x_new.copy() — no snapping of touching slots to Z! I add blockers with a == alpha == 1.0 — cands contains only p_s<0 slots with a_s == 1.0, added to Z with x=0.0. But x = x_new.copy() then `x[tgt[1]] = 0.0` overwrites ✓. OK.
